utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, let's get going, I know Bashir has a hard stop at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yep. Eleven sharp.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So, a couple of things. Audit events for billing, that's the main one. And the on-call swap.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, before we start, did anyone see Rania's email about the staging freeze?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Rania's, uh, I saw the subject line. Something about Thursday?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe it's Wednesday night through Thursday morning. I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, Wednesday. Fine. We don't have a deploy planned anyway, right?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not unless somebody sneaks one in.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Nobody's sneaking. Okay, audit events. So compliance has been asking where these live, and right now they're just, you know, log lines.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Log lines that rotate after thirty days.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Right, which is the problem. Sunita from compliance wants something queryable, and kept for a lot longer.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: How much longer, do we know?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Seven years was the number floating around. I'd have to double check that.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Seven is standard.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Okay so, I've been thinking about this since Monday, and honestly I'd just put them in the database we already have. A table, append-only, no updates, no deletes, and partition it by month so old stuff is easy to detach and archive. That's what I'd want.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Hang on, append-only how? Like enforced, or just by convention?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Enforced. Revoke update and delete from the service account, only insert. I did that on the old ledger thing at my last place.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Mm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So that's, um, the big picture, one table, same database.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah. And the reason it's attractive is, well, there's nothing new to stand up. No new cluster, no new on-call thing, nobody has to learn anything.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's true, I guess.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And the other thing, when compliance asks which invoice an event belongs to, you just join. It's the same database, so it's one query, not two systems stitched together.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sure, but how big does it get? That's the thing I'd worry about.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: So we're at about four million events a month, right? Priya, that's your number from the dashboard.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I think it was closer to three point eight? Maybe four. It's around there.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, round it to four. And each row is tiny, so that's about three gigs a month. Three, maybe a bit more. Which is nothing. We have more than that in temp files.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Three a month, so what, thirty-something a year.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Roughly. Over seven years it's, uh, I'd have to get the calculator out, but it's not scary.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Not scary.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, devil's advocate. A table that only grows. What does that do to backups?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Detach old partitions, dump them to cold storage. That's the whole point of the monthly split.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And vacuum? Or whatever, index bloat?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Append-only, so there's basically nothing to vacuum. It's the nicest kind of table.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe the index thing is still worth a look? Like if we index by invoice and by time, that's two indexes on every insert.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: It's two. Two indexes on four million a month is, I mean, that's like one or two a second. The database won't notice.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Agree.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, but what about the noisy neighbor angle. If audit writes spike, they're hitting the same box as the invoice stuff.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Is that a real worry? Like has it spiked before?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Month end. Everything spikes at month end.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Month end it's maybe three times normal. Still tiny.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I could pull the month-end numbers if we want. I think I have them from the capacity review.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: That'd be good, Priya, but I don't want to hold things up on it.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No, no, of course. I'll just send it around.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fine. Someone has to say it, and I said it.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Appreciated, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Switching for a sec. Gabor pinged me about the load test environment. Does anyone know who owns that now?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Nikos.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Nikos, right, I thought it moved to Nikos. Okay, I'll ask him.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Speaking of Nikos, did you all hear about his bike thing? He rode to the office in the rain, from, what, twenty kilometers away, and then realized he left his badge at home.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Of course he did.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And so Irina had to let him in, and they got talking, and it turns out Irina used to race. Like properly, in a club. She did a thing in the hills outside Brno, one of those long climbs where you can't even see the top.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Oh, that's interesting, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah and she said the trick is you never look up, you just look at the wheel in front of you. Which, I mean, is kind of good advice for most things.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Pavel, I love it, but we have Bashir for another twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, right. Sorry. Tangent.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Ten minutes now, actually.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Back to audit events. Before I decide anything, is there anyone who thinks the table is a bad idea outright?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not outright. I'd want to see the month-end numbers, but I'm not going to die on it.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe, um, I'm fine with it. As long as someone writes down the retention bit.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: The retention. Right. Meaning, how long we keep the detached partitions.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes. And where they go.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I'll write that up. Seven years, cold storage bucket, some kind of checksum.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Do we need Sunita to sign off on the bucket?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Probably. I'll send her the design when it exists.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Good. Sanne also had a question, something about whether the events carry the user's email.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: They shouldn't.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: They carry a user id. Not the email.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, that was Sanne's question, so I'll tell her. User id only.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And if someone deletes a user, for privacy?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: The id stays, the user record goes. Compliance has been okay with that before.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Has been. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Alright. I'm hearing a lot of comfort and a few small asks. Month-end numbers, the retention doc, Sunita on the bucket. Nobody is saying stop.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Then it's decided. Audit events go into the monthly-partitioned table in our existing database, and we'll build against that.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Great. I'll start on the schema tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Perfect. Not urgent urgent, but this sprint if you can.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Who's reviewing the grants part? The revoke stuff?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Me.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Thanks, Bashir. Okay, the on-call swap. Priya, you asked about trading the week of the twenty-third?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, yes, I think maybe, if it's okay. I have a family thing and I wasn't sure if it clashed.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I can take the twenty-third. I'm free.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Oh, really? That's, um, thank you. I can take your week in July then.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Sure. Whichever one it is.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'll update the sheet, just remind me which July week.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: The seventh, I think. Or the fourteenth. I'll check.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, send me the actual one.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Gotta go.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Yep, go, go. Thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Morning. Is everyone here? I don't see Pavel yet.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Here, here. My headset decided to update itself.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Priya, did you work out which July week you're covering for Kofi?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, yes. I think maybe it's the fourteenth. I checked the sheet last night.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I had the seventh in my head.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: The seventh is Bashir's, I'm fairly sure.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Great, fourteenth it is. Kofi, shout if that's wrong.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Next, Gabor asked about the load test environment again. Nikos says it's free next week.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Oh good. Because last time I used it the seed data was from like March.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: For invoice tests, kind of. Half the customers in there are on plans we retired.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So can someone ask Nikos to refresh it? Pavel?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll ping him after this.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Does a refresh wipe the dashboards? It did last time.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I don't think so. It might have. I'll ask.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fine. Okay, Priya, you said you had something from the audit side.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, yes. I talked to Sunita on Monday, about how long we have to keep these events, and, I think maybe it's bigger than we figured.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: More than seven years?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No, seven's right, but it's not a guideline. The auditors put it in writing, so it's required. And at our growth that's roughly two hundred fifty gigs sitting in the table.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And, um, I asked Irina about the backups. The nightly one on the primary is forty minutes now, and she thinks maybe ninety-five in about three years with all that in there. The maintenance window is only sixty.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Huh. Ninety-five. Okay, that's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: So that's what I was poking at last week. All seven years living on the primary means the backup runs out of its window, and the failover drills restore from that same backup, so those crawl too.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Well, hang on. The old partitions are static. The backup could in theory skip them, I'd have to check how we do it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Could in theory. Is that what we do today?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: No. Today it's the whole thing. Full dump.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe that's worth looking into? I'm not sure how much work it is.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Right, so, big picture, the table is still the plan, but this is a real wrinkle. Nobody's saying otherwise?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'm saying it's a wrinkle, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Priya, is Irina's estimate a guess?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, it was more of a back-of-envelope. I could ask her to run it properly against a copy.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Please. Not urgent, but soon.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask her today.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Funny thing, Irina told me last month the backup already runs long at month end because of the invoice runs.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fifty-something? Don't quote me.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: That's already close to the window.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Close, yeah. Sorry, I forgot that until just now.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Noted.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, let's park it until Irina's numbers come back. Anything else on that?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not from me.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Good. Other thing, and Bashir this one's yours, the pager last week was awful.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: People were saying the slow-query alerts were basically constant. Is that the database side?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes. It's too twitchy. Move it up to five hundred, from two hundred.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Why that much, though?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Sixty-three pages last week. Fifty-eight were the nightly report job. Nobody cares about those.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: The report job is just slow by nature, right? It scans everything.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe we'd still catch the real ones at that level? Like anything customer-facing would be well over it anyway.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Right. Real ones are way over.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, what if a real one creeps from two hundred to four hundred and nobody notices?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Dashboard shows it. Alert is for pages.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: We could also exclude the report job from the alert entirely. I did that at my old company, with a tag.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Later. Threshold first.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, that's reasonable. The slow-query alert goes to five hundred milliseconds.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I'll push the change today.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Thanks. Who gets paged if it does fire?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Whoever's on call. Kofi this week.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Yep, that's me till Friday.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Sanne asked whether we can move the Thursday sync, she has a clash.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: To when?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: She suggested Friday morning. I told her I'd check.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, Friday morning I have the, I think maybe the vendor call? Not sure of the time.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: What time is it?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Ten. Or ten thirty.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, so Friday at eleven works?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I can do eleven. Actually, I might have a thing with Nikos, but I can move it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, I'll tell her eleven. If it moves again I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: One more, Rania sent the quarterly planning template. Has anyone opened it?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Briefly.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: It's longer than last quarter.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: There's a new section on risks, I think? Um, I saw something.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'll skim it. Probably I'd want everyone's top three by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Top three of what?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Of what you want to work on. Big picture stuff, not tickets.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And the audit thing goes in there somewhere, I guess.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Probably, yes, depending on where we end up.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I have a hard stop. Need to go.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Go, go. Thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Morning all. Before the real stuff, the planning template. Anyone sent me their top three yet?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not yet. I've got two and a half.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I have like seven, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Seven isn't three, Pavel.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I know, I know. I'll cut it down.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe I have three? But one of them is sort of two things.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: That's fine, just send them by Monday. Doesn't need to be polished.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Monday.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Yes. Next, the Thursday sync that moved to Friday, did that stick? Sanne said eleven was fine.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I got the invite, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Me too, although it landed on top of my thing with Nikos, which I did move.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Good. And did the load test environment get refreshed?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Partly. Nikos redid the seed data, but the dashboards are gone. So it does wipe them.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Told you.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: You did. I'll rebuild them, they're not complicated.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Export them first next time.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah. Fair.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Audit events. Priya, did Irina ever get to the backup run against a copy?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, sort of. She did it on a smaller copy and then scaled it up, so I think maybe it's still an estimate.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Where did it land?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Somewhere around ninety, ninety-five minutes by year three. So about what she said before.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Against a sixty-minute window.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And I never checked whether the dump can skip the old partitions. I meant to. It's on my list, which is the list that's seven things long.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Let me say where my head is. Seven years is a written requirement, and the backup window is what it is, so I'd like to open the storage question again. Not to undo everything, just to look at it properly.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Fine by me. I've been waiting for that.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Can I just say, the table is still the right core. The joins to invoices, the grants, none of that goes away.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Nobody said it goes away.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: No, I know. I just want that on the record before the pile-on.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: There's no pile-on, I think maybe?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So as I understand it, it's everything in the table forever, or the old stuff goes somewhere else. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Kind of. I wrote the cold storage bit in the doc, but as more of a someday thing.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: When's someday? And who runs it?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: A script. Monthly, I figured.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Run by whom, and what pages when it fails?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Okay, I hadn't got that far.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe the auditors would want proof it actually ran, too?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Right, and that the copy matches.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: That's the checksum thing. Which I did put in.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Bashir, you've been quiet. Where are you on this?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Keep the table. Once a month closes, that partition gets exported every night, and we only hold ninety days hot.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Seven years of cold storage is about five bucks a month. And the auditors emailed back, checksummed exports in an open columnar format are fine.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Wait, they said that in writing?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Email.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Who was it, Sunita?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Sunita forwarded it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay, that's different from last week, when all we had was "required".

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, and honestly that's the same thing I said, it's just got a schedule on it.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: It's not though. You had it as a someday. This one's every night.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fine, fine. It's a better version of mine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And the ninety days, that fixes the backup thing?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Table stays small. A quarter's worth.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So the dump is only a quarter then? Um, instead of seven years.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, what if an auditor wants something from year four on short notice?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Query the files.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: With what?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Anything that reads that format. Lots of things do, even a laptop.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: And joining to the invoice?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Not as pretty. You'd load it into a scratch table, I mean, it's rare.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Rare.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I think maybe someone should test a restore once? Before we say it works.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes. Will do.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Who's building the export job?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Hold on, assignments after. Anyone actually against it? Kofi?

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Not against. The failure alert is what I care about. Silent failure is how you end up with a gap in year five.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fair. Pavel?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I'm fine. The object storage thing reminds me, Nikos told me how his old place lost a year of exports because the bucket had a lifecycle rule nobody remembered. It quietly deleted anything older than ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Ouch.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah, and they only found out because someone's cousin, no, a contractor, asked for an old file. And the guy who set the rule had left, and the rule was named after a ticket number, not what it did.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Oh no.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And then they spent two weeks going through logs. Which, anyway, is a bit of a story, but-

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Pavel, it's a good one, but-

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, sorry. The point is, no lifecycle rules that delete. Ever.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Agree.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Put that in the doc. Okay. Priya?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe I'm good with it, as long as the restore test happens before we call it done.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, I'm making the call. We keep the monthly-partitioned table in our database, only the last ninety days stay in it, and each night the closed partitions get exported out to object storage.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Great, I'll update the design doc today.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Alert on export failure goes in the doc too.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Yes, thanks Kofi.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I'll do the restore test.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Who owns the export job?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I'll take it. Bashir reviews, like the grants.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Sunita should see the final shape, since it was her thread.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I can send her the doc once Pavel's done? Um, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, different thing. Gabor asked whether anyone's on the release call Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: I'm on call, so I'll be around anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Good, you're the rep.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Great. Always me.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Rania's also asking about headcount for the planning doc. I told her we wouldn't have an answer till the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Are we asking for headcount?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm not sure yet. Probably one, depending on what the risks section says.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What's in the risks section? Um, I only skimmed it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Honestly mostly boxes to tick. I'll go through it with each of you.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Can I put the audit job in as a risk?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Put it as work, not as a risk.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Does Irina need to know about the new backup plan? Since it changes her window numbers.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Yes. Priya, can you tell her it may get smaller?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes, I'll mention it. I think maybe she'll want to rerun the estimate.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Maybe, don't push on it.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Not needed. It's smaller.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay, point taken, tell her anyway so she isn't surprised.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: Is the Friday sync still on? I forgot to ask.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Eleven, yes.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Should we put audit on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Just a quick update. Pavel, you can do two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Two minutes. I can do two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Kofi
utterances.text: You've never done two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, no, I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Thanks everyone. I need to jump to another call.
